title: Portable and Wireless Charging Solutions
desc: Understand power banks, wireless pads and shared charging kiosks: safety, standards, battery care and a simple service business.
outcomes: Explain how batteries, chargers and wireless pads work.
task: Test and compare three portable chargers, write a safety and quality note, and plan a small shared charging point with price and care rules.
condition: Three chargers (practice or real), a meter or phone app, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor. No opening of battery packs.
standard: Capacity test is repeated and averaged; safety rules are followed; unsafe items are rejected; business plan shows costs; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Shop owners, repair techs, event hosts, students.
evidence: test table, safety note, price sheet, plan
modules: Batteries, units and capacity
Understand
You cannot compare power banks without understanding the units.
Energy in watt-hours: Wh = volts x amp-hours; a 10,000 mAh cell at 3.7 V holds 37 Wh.
Conversion to 5 V and charging loses 20 to 40 per cent as heat.
Cycles of charge and discharge age batteries.
Labels often give capacity at cell voltage, not usable output.
A 37 Wh bank with 70 per cent efficiency delivers about 26 Wh, enough for roughly two charges of a 12 Wh phone.
Calculate usable energy for three banks from their labels.
Maths correct and assumptions stated.
Wired charging standards
Understand
Cables and plugs affect speed and safety.
Connector types and power delivery levels.
Thin cables overheat and limit current.
Match charger, cable and device.
Use certified products from reliable sellers.
A 65 W charger with a cheap cable charges a laptop slowly because the cable cannot carry the current.
Make a compatibility table for five devices.
Entries are correct.
Wireless charging
Understand
Coils and magnetic fields transfer energy without a plug.
Pad and device must align; metal objects between can heat up.
Efficiency is lower than wired charging; more heat.
Standards exist for compatibility.
Good for convenience, not always for speed.
A wireless pad at 70 per cent efficiency wastes 30 per cent as heat, so a 15 Wh phone charge draws about 21 Wh from the wall.
Explain how wireless charging works to a peer.
Peer can repeat the main idea and one limit.
Testing real capacity
Apply
Measure, do not trust the label.
Discharge fully into a known load while recording watt-hours with a meter.
Repeat three times and average.
Compare with the label and note the percentage.
Record temperature and time.
A 20,000 mAh bank labelled 74 Wh delivers 55 Wh, 74 per cent of the claim.
Test three banks and record results in a table.
Results recorded with averages and percentage of label.
Safety and quality
Evaluate
Poor batteries can overheat or catch fire.
Look for certification marks and protection circuits.
Avoid swollen, hot or damaged units.
Follow airline and transport rules for carrying batteries.
Dispose of faulty batteries at a collection point.
A swollen bank is isolated in a safe container away from flammable items and taken to a collection point.
Write a safety note and a disposal procedure.
Includes inspection, isolation and disposal.
A shared charging service
Create
Kiosks and lending services can serve events and cafes.
Locations: cafes, events, transport hubs.
Pricing by time or deposit.
Return, cleaning and loss control.
Staff training and insurance.
A cafe rents banks for 50 INR with a refundable deposit of 300 INR and tracks serial numbers.
Plan a small service with prices.
Costs and prices shown with currency.
Care, reuse and recycling
Apply
Extend the life of your devices.
Avoid heat; store at about half charge.
Recycle at collection points.
Repair only with trained people.
Label and track batteries.
A cafe has a labelled battery recycling box and a monthly collection.
Write care rules.
Rules are specific.
Pilot and review
Create
Test the idea for a week.
Run a trial with a small number of users.
Record use and complaints.
Improve based on data.
Decide whether to continue.
Week one: 40 rentals and 2 losses; a deposit is added and losses stop.
Present your review.
Numbers are real.
quiz: Formula for Wh?
Volts x amp-hours. (Covered in module 1: Batteries and units. To pass that module: Maths correct.)
Why losses?
Conversion and heat. (Covered in module 2: Wired charging standards. To pass that module: Entries correct.)
What marks safe goods?
Certification marks and protection circuits. (Covered in module 3: Wireless charging. To pass that module: Peer understands.)
What do you do with a swollen bank?
Isolate and dispose safely. (Covered in module 4: Testing capacity. To pass that module: Results recorded.)
Wireless pad efficiency issue?
Lower efficiency, more heat. (Covered in module 5: Safety and quality. To pass that module: Includes disposal.)
Why store at half charge?
Slows ageing. (Covered in module 6: Shared charging service. To pass that module: Costs and prices shown.)
How measure capacity?
Discharge into a known load and measure Wh. (Covered in module 7: Care and recycling. To pass that module: Rules specific.)
Why repeat tests?
To average errors. (Covered in module 8: Plan and review. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
Name a loss control.
Deposit. (Covered in module 8: Plan and review. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
Where recycle batteries?
Collection points. (Covered in module 8: Plan and review. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
